# Uniform ranges

Uniform integers and floats in a bounded range.

<h2 id="uniform-below"><code>UniformBelow&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UniformBelow<G: RandomGenerator>(
    generator: &var G,
    bound: uint64
) -> uint64
```

A uniform value in `[0, bound)`.
A bound of zero has no values to choose from and gives zero, which is the only answer that is not a lie.
Runs in constant expected time; the loop below runs more than once with probability under `bound / 2^64`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Uniform.rux#L22)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type     | Description               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from  |
| `bound`     | `uint64` | the exclusive upper bound |

**Returns**: a value in `[0, bound)`, each equally likely and with no modulo bias

<h2 id="uniform-in-range"><code>UniformInRange&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UniformInRange<G: RandomGenerator>(
    generator: &var G,
    low: uint64,
    high: uint64
) -> uint64
```

A uniform value in `[low, high]`, both ends included.
Inclusive because that is what a caller asking for a die roll or a random index into a known last element
means. `low` above `high` is an empty range and gives `low`. The full range of the type is representable:
a span of every value is a bound of 2^64, which does not fit in a `uint64`, and is handled as its own case
rather than by an arithmetic accident.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Uniform.rux#L49)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type     | Description               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from  |
| `low`       | `uint64` | the inclusive lower bound |
| `high`      | `uint64` | the exclusive upper bound |

**Returns**: a value in `[low, high)`, each equally likely

<h2 id="uniform-in-signed-range"><code>UniformInSignedRange&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UniformInSignedRange<G: RandomGenerator>(
    generator: &var G,
    low: int64,
    high: int64
) -> int64
```

A uniform signed value in `[low, high]`, both ends included.
The span is computed in unsigned arithmetic, so a range crossing zero — or spanning the whole width, where
the difference of the ends overflows a signed type — is ordinary rather than a special case.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Uniform.rux#L68)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type     | Description               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from  |
| `low`       | `int64`  | the inclusive lower bound |
| `high`      | `int64`  | the exclusive upper bound |

**Returns**: a value in `[low, high)`, each equally likely

<h2 id="uniform-float-in-range"><code>UniformFloatInRange&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UniformFloatInRange<G: RandomGenerator>(
    generator: &var G,
    low: float64,
    high: float64
) -> float64
```

A uniform `float64` in `[low, high)`.
The interval is half-open at the top, matching [`NextFloat64`](/docs/api/random/random-generator#next-float64). A reversed pair gives `low`, and an interval so
wide that its span overflows to an infinity gives values across the whole of it rather than a NaN.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Uniform.rux#L84)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description               |
| ----------- | --------- | ------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G`  | where the bits come from  |
| `low`       | `float64` | the inclusive lower bound |
| `high`      | `float64` | the exclusive upper bound |

**Returns**: a value in `[low, high)`
